text:
Maya: quick heads-up — ran the seedset holdout for probebird-v1 on short-tail queries. recall@10 fell from 0.88 -> 0.72 after we started L2-normalizing embeddings. not sure if it's whitening/scale or the seed composition.
Oliver: ugh that gap is big. did you compare cosine vs raw l2?
Maya: yes, cosine with L2-norm is what produced the 0.72. raw (no norm) gives ~0.86 on the same holdout.
Sophie: can you paste exact eval command and seedset? might be an input preprocessing mismatch.
Maya: command I ran:
```bash
python eval/recall.py --model probebird-v1 --seedset data/seed_shorttail.jsonl --holdout holdout_shorttail.jsonl --norm l2 --k 10 --metric cosine
```
Maya: seedset is the usual shorttail seed (500 queries, boosted exact-match examples).
Liam: two quick hypotheses: 1) model changed output scale (norm interacts with whitening/centroids), 2) holdout contains many near-duplicates where raw dot correlates better.
Evan: also consider quantization differences — are you testing fp16 only? int6/int8 could amplify small shifts.
Maya: this run was fp16. I have an int6 quantized build queued as well. infra-bot: job 62219 completed — full similarity matrix up at https://ci.internal/62219 (artifact: probebird-v1_shorttail_recall.tar.gz) :white_check_mark:
Oliver: can we quickly check recall@1 and median rank? sometimes recall@10 masks rank shifts.
Maya: recall@1 dropped 0.61 -> 0.45, median rank went from 3 -> 12. so it's not just tails.
Sophie: try two controlled runs: A) force no normalization (postproc identity) B) l2-normalize + per-batch whitening (learned mean/std from train) and compare. also run cosine vs dot in both.
Liam: I'll run A locally against the holdout to confirm raw behavior. if raw matches previous, it's postproc order bug.
Evan: I'll spin the int6 eval on the same holdout to see quant amplification. recommend batchsize=128 to match serving.
Maya: thanks — planning to run three experiments in parallel:
- exp1: raw embeddings (no norm), cosine and dot
- exp2: l2-normalize then whitening, cosine and dot
- exp3: fp16 vs int6 compare (same postproc as exp1)
Maya: small snippet to reproduce (paste into runbook):
```bash
# eval script
python eval/recall.py \
  --model probebird-v1 \
  --holdout holdout_shorttail.jsonl \
  --seedset data/seed_shorttail.jsonl \
  --k 10 \
  --save-output out/probebird_v1_shorttail.jsonl \
  --postproc none|l2|whiten \
  --quant none|int6|fp16 
```
infra-bot: job 62245 queued (exp3: probebird-v1 int6) — ETA ~18m
Oliver: one more note — our index uses L2 distance after normalizing vectors in the ingest pipeline. if we change query-time norm only, we may get asymmetric behavior. make sure ingest and query postproc are matched.
Sophie: good catch. add a test where we re-index one small shard with the new postproc and run the same holdout. should be quick with 50k passages.
Liam: re-indexing shard now -> will post results.
Evan: if re-index + l2 norm still bad, we should try center-crop whitening (subtract global mean) rather than scaling variance — sometimes that recovers rank.
Maya: agreed. goal for today: identify whether drop is due to postproc mismatch, seed composition, or quant. plan: collect exp1/exp2/exp3 results, re-index a mini-shard, and reconvene here with numbers. I'll open a short PR with the eval commands and expected outputs.
Sophie: I'll own the whitening experiment and the re-index.
Oliver: I'll audit seedset composition (duplicates/boosts) and run a parity test across previous model revision.
Liam: will paste quick raw-run results in ~10m.
Maya: thanks team — tagging @Sophie @Oliver @Liam @Evan. i'll pin artifacts to the ticket (ML-8763). :eyes:
infra-bot: job 62245 finished — int6 run artifact at https://ci.internal/62245/int6_report.html (summary: recall@10=0.69)
Maya: int6 shows 0.69 (worse than fp16 but not as bad as l2+cosine). putting findings into the PR.
Sophie: initial whitened+re-index run shows recall@10=0.85, recall@1=0.58 — looks promising.
Oliver: sounds like centering/whitening fixed the shift; likely new model mean drift. we should add a small normalization step in the onboarding checklist.
Maya: action items recorded: 1) add mean-subtraction check to onboarding evals, 2) include index+query postproc parity test, 3) include int6 regression check for short-tail. I'll update ML-8763 and close this triage after final artifacts. :thumbsup:
Evan: great. once PR is up I can test the serving path with batchsize 256 and measure latency impact.
Maya: perfect — thanks everyone.
